name: Outdoor Stage Two-Person Ability Show
description: Develops a character description, ability type, stage scene or climax structure into an audience first-person outdoor stage two-person ability duel short, advancing in stages through the creative specification, storyboard, key elements, single-shot video and audio layers.

planning.planning_notes: Dynamic execution path: first judge the entry point from aspect_ratio, resolution, venue_type, vo_language, the user's character/ability description and the canvas assets. Before any generation node, organize the creative specification at the Skill level, locking each video at 15 seconds, one video corresponding to one shot, the two characters A/B, both sides' abilities, stage positioning, the conflict relationship, aspect ratio, resolution, outdoor stage realism and narration language; this specification creates no standalone node. If the user gives only one character, you must first complete or propose a second original opponent/partner, and must not directly make a solo ability showcase. After the specification is organized, create the storyboard: design only 1 shot per video, using Beat 1 -> Beat 2 -> Beat 3 -> Beat 4 -> Final beat to write the internal escalation of a single take, without seconds or hard cuts. After the storyboard is complete, create the key element stage, and create independent key element nodes separately for independently referenceable assets: Character A, Character B, the complete outdoor stage / theater space, key props, and both sides' ability effect sources; do not create an audience POV asset. Do not merge multiple subjects into one key element overview image; only assets that are always referenced downstream as one whole may share a node. After the key elements are complete, create the single-shot videos, where each 15-second video references the confirmed Character A, Character B, the stage/scene and the necessary props/effect sources; generate only visuals first, without VO/BGM. After the visual videos are complete, create the audio layers, generating the VO and BGM prompts at once. Finally, automatically create the final composition node, wiring all single-shot videos and audio layers in playback order; BGM defaults to 0.7, VO defaults to 1.0, and each video fades out for 2 seconds at its end.
planning.prompt_guide: The core is an audience first-person view of a two-person supernatural performance/duel on an outdoor stage. The camera is like the viewer's eyes or a phone lens, but no phone body, recording interface, screen-in-screen or large centered phone may appear. By default it is not a professional camera position, drone, broadcast camera position or third-person cinematic shot. Each 15-second video is one continuous handheld long take, whose internal rhythm is written only as narrative beats, with no timestamps and no hard cut/switch angle/new shot. The characters must look like real stage performers / stunt performers, with real human proportions, cloth wrinkles, leather/metal/armor texture and props with weight; ability effects must be translated into stage lighting, smoke, fire rings, LED light curtains, light beams, shockwaves, projections and live post-enhancement.
conduct_rules: Default to two characters A/B; when the user gives only one character, a second original opponent/partner must be completed or asked for, and a solo ability show must not be the default.

If the user mentions a well-known anime/game character, it may only serve as inspiration; official character names, work titles, move names, organization names, village names, signature lines, emblems or patterns must not be written in the storyboard or prompts.
Each 15-second video corresponds to only 1 shot; internal escalation uses Beat 1/2/3/4/Final beat, not seconds, and is not split into multiple shots.

The key element stage must be split into multiple independent nodes, containing at least Element_Character_A, Element_Character_B and the complete stage space; if both sides' ability effect sources, core props or special stage devices need to be referenced across shots, they must also each be their own node. The audience POV is a shot constraint, not a separate asset.

The Shot must use a three-layer composition: foreground audience heads/shoulders/arms/a few edge phones, midground stage and the two characters, background outdoor theater buildings/lighting rigs/banners/sky/smoke layers.
Every Beat must keep the other character as a target, defender, reactor or spatial anchor, and must not become two independent showcases.
Hit feedback must be specific to center of gravity, footwork, shielding the face, slide steps, bent knees, bracing and regaining balance; effects cannot replace the body reaction.
Audience reactions change by faction: when A has the upper hand, A's supporters cheer; when B counterattacks, the audience on the other side stands up, raises hands and shakes phones.
Video prompts default to no music and no subtitles; VO and BGM are generated separately only after the visual videos are complete.

rating_bands.description: The two-character stage relationship is clear, the audience POV long take is stable, and the three-layer composition, IP avoidance, stage effects, hit feedback, faction audience reactions and stage boundaries are all complete.
Basically fits a stage duel, but character B, the foreground audience, real stage texture, hit feedback, IP rewriting or staged audio handling has gaps.

Made into a solo ability showcase, a professional cinematic camera position, a third-person shot, hard-cut multiple shots, direct use of official IP, a centered phone screen recording, or a pure CG arena.

visual_review_items.name: Audience POV
visual_review_items.description: The shot must be a live long take like the viewer's eyes / phone lens, but must not show the recording device or interface.

visual_review_items.name: Two-character relationship
visual_review_items.description: A/B must share one stage coordinate system, with attack, defense, reaction and the climax happening between the two.

visual_review_items.name: Live realism
visual_review_items.description: The foreground audience, stage buildings, lighting and smoke, prop materials and body impact feedback must all be believable.

text_review_items.name: Single-shot rule
text_review_items.description: Each 15-second video corresponds to only 1 shot, using narrative beats internally, with no timestamps or hard cuts.

text_review_items.name: IP avoidance
text_review_items.description: Well-known characters must be turned into original stage performer settings, with official names, emblems and moves removed.

text_review_items.name: Audio separation
text_review_items.description: The video stage does not generate VO/BGM; a short VO and an instrumental / sound-effect BGM are generated after the visual videos are complete.

domain_constraints: Do not create an audience POV key element.
Do not use official anime/game character names, move names, organization names, emblems or signature lines.
Do not show a large centered phone, recording UI, screen-in-screen, third-person cinematic camera position, drone shots, hard cuts or multi-shot switching.
